title_en: Fragment on the Second Letter to the Thessalonians
author: Gennadius of Constantinople
occasion: The fragment comments on 2 Thessalonians 2:7-8, explaining the timing and manner of the revelation of the lawless one in relation to God's appointed limit.
argument: Gennadius states that when the end of God's appointed time arrives, and the present restraining boundary is removed, having been fulfilled, then the lawless one will be revealed immediately and without any delay.

outline.move: The whole fragment states that when God's appointed limit is reached and the present restraining boundary is removed, the lawless one will be revealed at once without delay.

cast.name: the lawless one
cast.who: The figure whose revelation is being restrained until God's appointed time.

key_terms.sense: The lawless one whose future revelation is being discussed

scripture: The source title uses the Latin form 'epistulam ii ad Thessalonicenses' (with Roman numeral 'ii'), rendered in English as 'the Second Epistle to the Thessalonians'. _unresolved_facts.claim: explaining the timing and manner of the revelation of the lawless one in relation to God's appointed limit
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὅταν μέντοι τὸ πέρας ἐπιστῇ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ προθεσμίας, καὶ ὁ νῦν κατέχων αὐτὸν ὅρος ἐκστῇ πληρωθείς, ἑτοίμως τότε καὶ δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς ὁ ἄνομος ἀποκαλυφθήσεται
_unresolved_facts.fix: The fragment states that when the end of God's appointed time arrives and the present restraining boundary is removed, having been fulfilled, then the lawless one will be revealed immediately and without any delay. The source does not explicitly discuss 'timing and manner' as analytical categories; this is interpretive elaboration.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Gennadius states that when the end of God's appointed time arrives, and the present restraining boundary is removed, having been fulfilled, then the lawless one will be revealed immediately and without any delay
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὁ νῦν κατέχων αὐτὸν ὅρος ἐκστῇ πληρωθείς
_unresolved_facts.fix: The text says ὅρος (boundary/limit), not 'boundary' as a person or power. The brief's rendering 'restraining boundary' obscures that this is an unusual reading—the standard biblical text has ὁ κατέχων (the one who restrs) as a masculine personal participle, but this fragment reads ὅρος (neuter noun, 'boundary/limit'). The brief should note this textual variant rather than assimilating it to the standard interpretation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The source title uses the Latin form 'epistulam ii ad Thessalonicenses' (with Roman numeral 'ii')
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Fragmentum in epistulam ii ad Thessalonicenses
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source uses lowercase 'ii' not Roman numeral 'II'. More importantly, the source consistently uses 'ii' (lower case), and the brief's claim about 'Roman numeral' is inaccurate—'ii' is not a Roman numeral form in the source (which would be 'II').

_unresolved_facts.claim: The source also contains the notation '2 Thess 2,78', which appears to be a typographical error or unusual notation in the source (likely intended as 2:7-8 or 2:7,8)
_unresolved_facts.fix: The notation '2,78' is not standard but the brief's parenthetical '(likely intended as 2:7-8 or 2:7,8)' is speculative. The comma notation '2,78' could represent chapter 2, verses 7-8 in a continental European numbering system, or it could be an error. The brief should simply note the notation as it appears without speculating on 'likely' intentions, or note multiple possibilities.
